title: Some gamers want zero AI in games to protect developers’ jobs and keep game development “pure”, but some devs say this attitude is actually hurting them. What do you think?
author: Tactical_10

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body: I think this conversation is boring and has no place in this sub, or any dev subs to be fair, considering that it's never constructive or backed by real sources outside of "trust me bro" and arbitrary numbers pulled out of someone's behind just to support their argument one way or the other.

comments.author: roodammy44
comments.body:
I don't think this is realistic. AI has changed all programming forever, which I can tell you as a programmer, sucks.

What will make a difference is whether something is good or not. There's multiple as many times apps on app stores recently but the amount of apps downloaded is actually falling, probably the deluge of slop is even drowning out the quality apps.

There's even more competition out there than ever so only the highest quality will win.

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body: I think it's to protect artist, and people scared for them. Also most AI art is sourced from chatgpt and it has a certain messy look to it people are tired of.

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body: it looks like that because people dont know how to make it look different, they take the first thing they get

replies.author: crowieforlife
replies.body: If a dev is too lazy to even try prompting AI well, that doesn't inspire in me trust that their game isn't slop.

replies.author: zayelion
replies.body: I'm sitting through an art clean up atm. Its ran for 16hrs. All aspects of this take a long time and there just has not been enough time passed. Most games take 6  plus months. The effective tools are only about 4 months old.

replies.author: crowieforlife
replies.body: At least you're cleaning it up, most people don't even do that. That's how we get characters with 10 fingers.

comments.author: BadgerPast4204
comments.body: Es simple, una IA hace que un desarrollador en solitario pueda crear un juego, más desarrolladores = a más juegos, claro que esto inclementa la basura, ahora la gente está jugando con la IA aun q cada vez menos, entiendo que en grandes producciones esté peor visto, pero es por desconocimiento, un artista que usa la IA bien de echo dibuja, y entre en una comunidad que aboga por el uso de una IA ética y por su dignificación, reitero es una tecnología que llegó para quedarse, así que podemos usarla para bien o para mal, pero que se usará se usará

comments.author: Advanced_Invite9435
comments.body: I use to do textilies and I was too lazy to learn all the big fancy equipment when I was in college. I made excuses I wanted my work to be pure. Lol

comments.author: Upbeat-Mail7201
comments.body: Most gamers are absolutely delusional and it's growing each year 😅

comments.author: ipreuss
comments.body:
Boycotting AI won’t prevent big studios from using it and firing developers but will harm indie developers.  

Essentially AI has fuelled the growth of indie developers.  Currently there’s a lot of slop because it’s quick to produce, but we’re already seeing the first releases from indie developers who invest time in creating high-quality content that wouldn’t have been feasible without AI.

comments.author: hikotv
comments.body:
It's like the same people who want to "protect" artists by hindering their use of AI so they can't work fast and efficiently and instead need to work on a revision for a week until they can send it in for further feedback. Actual artists have grinded for decades, they don't need to prove anything, but they are still kept shackled by their supposed helpers and supporters, who in fact, couldn't give two fks about how hard you work or how much goes into it, the label is the only thing that matters to them.

Like others have mentioned, naturally there will be a lot of slop by those without prior skills and knowledge, as well as those who are trying to cash in on AI, but that's just a natural byproduct of progression in an industry sense. 

All you can do is work on yourself, learn, practice, and use any new tool that seems like an upgrade to your workflow, only you know and care how much work goes into it.
